John Ternus officially took over as Apple's CEO this week, and the Financial Times published a feature interview today revealing details about Ternus's life and his reputation among Apple employees and partners.

Latest John Ternus interview reveals more details about Apple's new CEO

John Ternus becomes Apple's new CEO, taking over just days after Tim Cook transitioned to the role of Executive Chairman.

9to5Mac editor-in-chief Chance Miller compiled a detailed article covering everything we know about Ternus so far, including his educational background, early career, and public remarks.

However, the latest interview published by the Financial Times today adds more new details and observations to the story.

Regarding Ternus's reputation inside Apple, the report noted that he is known within the company as "extremely capable but low-key." A major Apple supplier partner echoed this assessment:

However, a former Apple executive told the Financial Times that Ternus "is relatively unknown outside the hardware division" within the company. Nevertheless, it is unclear how long ago the executive left Apple, and Ternus's presence within the company has clearly grown over the past year.

Tim Cook previously stated that Apple "wants this transition to be the best it can be." According to an anecdote in the interview, the transition has indeed received similar praise internally.

In addition, the Financial Times also revealed several details about Ternus's private life in the interview. According to the report, he is married with children, and was born and raised in California.

To learn more about Apple's new CEO, you can refer to our previous related coverage:

  • Who is John Ternus? Everything you need to know about Apple's next CEO
  • John Ternus makes his first appearance as Apple CEO, revealing his work priorities
  • Read the full internal memo John Ternus sent to Apple employees on his first day

We will get our first public glimpse of Ternus as CEO at Apple's major iPhone event next week.
